snip.t: An extrapleural approach means a leak stays contained and no chest drain is needed in some units.
Parapneumonic effusion and empyema: antibiotics plus chest drain if pus, pH below 7.2, positive Gram stain or culture, or loculation; fibrinolytics or surgical decortication if it fails.
Drain, do not just drug: a pleural pH below 7.2, pus or a positive culture needs a chest drain as well as antibiotics.
Tension pneumothorax: immediate needle decompression (large-bore cannula, 2nd intercostal space mid-clavicular line or 4th–5th space anterior axillary line), then a chest drain.
Large or breathless: needle aspiration (16–18G cannula, up to 2.5 L); if it fails, a small-bore chest drain.
Insert an intercostal chest drain attached to an underwater seal for empyema, haemothorax, or large pneumothoraces.
